details.overview: The International Society of Public Law (ICON•S) has announced a call for applications for the fifth edition of its Winter/Summer School for Junior Scholars, scheduled to take place from 17 to 27 May 2027 in Sydney, Australia. whoCanApply: Participants will be selected by a special ICON•S subcommittee. According to the announcement, the selection process will refer to principles of racial and geographic diversity and gender parity.

These principles indicate that the organizers intend to consider the composition of the selected group as part of the selection process. The program is designed to bring together a small group of junior scholars, making it important for applicants to present their academic background, research interests, and motivation clearly.

The announcement does not provide a numerical scoring system or a detailed ranking formula. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that selection depends on any single factor not explicitly stated by the organizers.

To prepare a strong application, candidates should ensure that their CV, cover letter, and research abstract present a coherent academic profile and demonstrate a clear reason for participating in the school.
The Winter/Summer School will take place in Sydney, Australia, so international participants may need an Australian visa depending on their nationality and circumstances.

The organizers state that applicants who need visas will receive invitation letters promptly after notification of acceptance. Instructions for requesting a visa letter will be included in the acceptance notification.

The requirement for an invitation letter depends on the applicant’s nationality and the type of visa being requested. Applicants should consult the Australian Government’s official visa information and determine which visa pathway applies to their situation.
benefits: The program offers several forms of support intended to reduce the cost of participating in the school in Sydney. However, applicants should distinguish between the costs explicitly covered by the organizers and expenses that may still need to be arranged independently.
Applicants may submit a financial aid statement if they wish to explain their need for financial support. This is listed as an optional document.

Applicants seeking a travel bursary should pay particular attention to the financial aid section and the relevant questions in the application form. They should clearly state whether they are requesting consideration for a bursary and whether receiving financial support is necessary for them to attend.
Research development: An opportunity to workshop a draft article or chapter and receive feedback from experienced mentors and peers.
Academic writing and publishing guidance: Sessions focused on skills relevant to developing and communicating scholarly research.
Mentorship: Opportunities to learn from established academics and reflect on future career plans.
Professional connections: The chance to meet other junior scholars and develop relationships within the ICON•S community.
howToApply: Applications must be submitted through Oxford Abstracts, the online platform used by ICON•S to receive and manage submissions. The same platform is also used for submissions to the 2027 ICON•S Annual Conference.
Applicants who have not previously used Oxford Abstracts may need to create an account. The announcement states that applicants can also log in through Google or LinkedIn.
The ICON•S Winter/Summer School may be especially valuable for junior scholars who want to strengthen their research and become more connected with the international academic community.

The announcement states that applications are open to all junior scholars and does not list a nationality-based restriction. Applicants should still check their eligibility and consider the Australian visa requirements that apply to their nationality.

Be interested in interdisciplinary research and the wider relevance of your work.
Have sufficient proficiency in English to conduct research, discuss your work, and participate fully in the program.
Be available to participate full-time and in person for the full program period (3 months, June, July & August)
benefits: Academic mentorship: Develop your project with guidance and feedback from IIASA researchers.
Interdisciplinary perspectives: Exchange ideas with scientists working across disciplines on global challenges.
Research and professional development: Build your knowledge and skills through the YSSP training program.
International connections: Become part of a cohort of around 50 doctoral researchers and connect with the wider IIASA community.
The YSSP is a three-month mentored research program. It consists of three aspects:

YSSP Training Program – tailored to early career researchers to build their skills and knowledge through seminars, workshops, and talks. It is expected that approximately 20% of your YSSP time will be spent on this aspect.
YSSP social program – helps participants build connections within their cohort and across the institute. It is expected that approximately 10% of your YSSP time will be spent on this aspect.
howToApply: Read the full call on the official page (iiasa.ac.at)
Prepare a short CV and a motivation statement
Submit the application before 10 January 2027
Start your visa appointment early once accepted — Ethiopian passports need visas for most hosts
